```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use a visitor's Snowflake account to query with DBI or dbplyr. The example
shows their Snowflake username and active role before you add your own SQL.

## Snowflake setup

Install `odbc` and the Snowflake ODBC driver. Ask your Snowflake administrator
for a [custom-client OAuth integration](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-custom)
with `http://localhost:8100` as the redirect URI. Use its client ID and
secret in the Shiny app. The requested role must be available to the users
signing in and have access to the warehouse and data.

For this local HTTP example, the administrator must allow the callback with
`OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE` in the development integration.
Use an HTTPS redirect URI when deploying. See the
[integration settings](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-security-integration-oauth-snowflake)
for this option and refresh-token settings.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_snowflake_client(
  server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
  role = "REPORTING_READER",
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_snowflake(
    auth$connection,
    server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
    role = "REPORTING_READER",
    warehouse = "REPORTING_WH",
    database = "ANALYTICS"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE()")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

Keep the server hostname and role consistent between the sign-in client and
the connection helper. Replace the warehouse and database with your own.

## Query a table

The returned connection works with ordinary DBI calls. For example, replace
the output with a query against your `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS` table:

```{r table-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS LIMIT 20")
})
```

Call `con()` before querying. The helper reuses the connection and closes it
when the authorization or Shiny session ends.

## Defaults and driver options

Set `schema = "PUBLIC"` on the connection helper to choose a default schema.
You can omit `warehouse`, `database`, and `schema` to use the account's
defaults. Set `driver` to the installed Snowflake ODBC driver name if it
differs from the default. See `?oauth_db_snowflake` for other options.

## External OAuth

If Snowflake trusts Entra, Okta, or another external issuer, configure a
shinyOAuth client for that issuer instead of using
`oauth_db_snowflake_client()`. It must request the audience and role scopes
accepted by your Snowflake integration.

Use the same `oauth_db_snowflake()` helper, passing `target` if the client
uses named token targets, and `required_scopes` matching the integration's
role scope. Native Snowflake OAuth derives that scope from `role` by default;
an external provider may use different names. See
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) for custom targets and scopes.
